lem-joint-gaussian-blocks-with-zero-cros:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(U_1,U_2)$ be a jointly multivariate-normal vector with mean $(m_1,m_2)$ and covariance
$$
\begin{pmatrix}S&0\\0&T\end{pmatrix},
$$
where $S$ and $T$ are allowed to be singular positive-semidefinite matrices. Then the random vectors $U_1$ and $U_2$ are independent.
thm-nondegenerate-multivariate-normal-la:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. If $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$, then its law has Lebesgue density
$$
f_{m,\Sigma}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2}
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-m)^T\Sigma^{-1}(x-m)\right),
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.
$$
def-error-contrast-matrix:
## Definition

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank, with $p<n$, and let $\operatorname{col}(X)^\perp$ denote the orthogonal complement of its column space in Euclidean $\mathbb R^n$ ([[def-orthogonal-complement]]). An **error-contrast matrix** for $X$ is a matrix $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-p)}$ whose columns form a basis of $\operatorname{col}(X)^\perp$. Thus $K$ has full column rank and $X^TK=0$, so $K^TY$ is an $(n-p)$-dimensional vector of linear contrasts that annihilate $X\beta$. Such a matrix exists by [[lem-error-contrast-matrix-exists]].

This column-basis convention makes the product $K^TY$ dimensionally defined. The Gaussian restricted-likelihood definition below fixes one such $K$ independently of the covariance parameter.
def-known-covariance-generalized-least-s:
## Definition

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank in a fixed-design first-moment regression model, so $\mathbb E_\beta Y=X\beta$ under each law $P_\beta$ ([[def-fixed-design-linear-regression-model]]). Suppose the same known symmetric positive-definite matrix $V$ is the covariance of $Y$ under every $P_\beta$. Put
$$
C=(X^T V^{-1}X)^{-1}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{GLS}}:=CX^T V^{-1}Y.
$$
This is a statistic and estimator of the identity target $\beta$ under [[def-statistic-and-estimator]] and [[def-estimand-on-a-statistical-model]]: for fixed $X$ and $V$, the displayed expression is a linear, hence Borel-measurable, function of the response. The positive definiteness of $X^TV^{-1}X$ and existence of its inverse are established by [[lem-gls-information-matrix-is-positive-definite]].

This definition uses the true covariance as known. Replacing $V$ by an estimate defines a plug-in procedure; the theorem below does not assign that procedure the same exact covariance or BLUE guarantee.
def-linear-mixed-model:
## Definition

Let $n,p\ge1$ and $q\ge0$ be finite integers. A **finite-dimensional linear mixed model** on one probability space consists of fixed matrices $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ and $Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, a fixed parameter $\beta\in\mathbb R^p$, and square-integrable random vectors $b\in\mathbb R^q$ and $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^n$ such that
$$
Y=X\beta+Zb+\varepsilon,\qquad \mathbb E b=0,\qquad \mathbb E\varepsilon=0,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(b)=G,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon)=R,
$$
where $b$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent random elements. Here $G$ and $R$ are the resulting symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance matrices. The fixed-design convention for $X$ and the first-moment regression model is that of [[def-fixed-design-linear-regression-model]]. The explicit scientific record of units, quantities, observation mechanism, and adequacy assumptions is required by [[def-scientific-statistical-model-contract]].

For longitudinal data, let $j$ index subjects and let $i\in S_j$ index the visits scheduled for subject $j$. A row of $Y$, $X$, and $Z$ corresponds to one observed subject–visit pair $(j,i)$; the time $t_{ji}$ is measured from a stated origin. Blocks of $b$ may represent subject-specific latent effects, while $R$ records the residual covariance across observed rows. If a visit pattern is fixed or conditioned on, the corresponding rows are selected from the scheduled vectors and matrices. If the pattern is random, its observation mechanism is specified separately; the displayed model does not assert that this mechanism is independent of the full outcomes or ignorable for likelihood inference.

The definition imposes no Gaussianity, no identical visit schedule, and no claim that a scientific application satisfies the proposed mean or covariance structure.
def-gaussian-linear-mixed-model:
## Definition

The **Gaussian branch** of [[def-linear-mixed-model]] adds the following assumption: under the Axiom of Choice, the concatenated vector
$$
W=\begin{pmatrix}b\\ \varepsilon\end{pmatrix}
$$
has the multivariate-normal law $N_{q+n}(0,\operatorname{diag}(G,R))$ of [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]. Thus the full latent-effect and residual vector is jointly Gaussian. This is an additional branch; the moment-only definition and the covariance identity do not assume Gaussianity.
def-longitudinal-missingness-mechanisms:
## Definition

Let $m=\sum_j|S_j|$ and let $Y^*\in\mathbb R^m$ be the complete scheduled response vector for subjects $j$ and visits $i$. Let the declared observed covariates take values in a measurable space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$. The finite set of observation patterns is $\mathcal R=\{0,1\}^m$; $r_{ji}=1$ means visit $(j,i)$ is observed. A missingness mechanism is a function $g:\mathcal R\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathcal X\to[0,1]$ such that, for every $(y^*,x)$, $\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}g(r\mid y^*,x)=1$, and, for each fixed $r$, $(y^*,x)\mapsto g(r\mid y^*,x)$ is measurable for $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^m)\otimes\mathcal A$. Thus $g(\cdot\mid y^*,x)$ is a probability mass function on $\mathcal R$, and its dependence on the full data state is the finite-output kernel specified by the observation-mechanism field in [[def-scientific-statistical-model-contract]], which requires a probability measure at each state and measurable state dependence. For a pattern $r$, write $Y_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ for the subvector of $Y^*$ at coordinates with $r_{ji}=1$.

The mechanism is **missing completely at random (MCAR)** if, for each pattern $r$, $g(r\mid y^*,x)$ does not depend on $y^*$. It is **missing at random (MAR)** if, for each $r$, it depends on the full response vector only through $Y_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ and $x$. It is **missing not at random (MNAR)** relative to this partition if the MAR condition fails for at least one pattern on the declared support. **Monotone dropout** means that, within each subject, observed visits form an initial segment of the scheduled visits, possibly empty or complete.

These are properties of the declared observation kernel. A mixed-model mean or covariance equation does not specify the kernel or imply MCAR, MAR, or MNAR.
lem-error-contrast-matrix-exists:
## Statement

For every full-column-rank $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with $p<n$, there exists an error-contrast matrix $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-p)}$ as defined in [[def-error-contrast-matrix]].
lem-gls-information-matrix-is-positive-d:
## Statement

If $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ has full column rank and $V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is symmetric positive definite, then $X^TV^{-1}X$ is symmetric positive definite. In particular it is invertible.
lem-marginal-covariance-of-linear-mixed-:
## Statement

For the moment model $Y=X\beta+Zb+\varepsilon$ of [[def-linear-mixed-model]], the marginal covariance is
$$
\operatorname{Cov}(Y)=V:=ZGZ^T+R.
$$
This identity uses only the stated means, covariances, and independence; it does not require Gaussianity.
lem-reml-error-contrast-covariance-is-po:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank with $p<n$, let $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-p)}$ be an error-contrast matrix for $X$, and let $V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite. Then $K^TVK$ is symmetric positive definite. No Gaussian assumption is needed for this matrix claim.
lem-gaussian-error-contrast-is-multivari:
## Statement

Assume AC and the Gaussian branch of the finite-dimensional mixed model. Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank with $p<n$, let $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-p)}$ be an error-contrast matrix, and let $V=ZGZ^T+R=\operatorname{Cov}(Y)$. Then
$$
K^TY\sim N_{n-p}(0,K^TVK).
$$
The contrast law does not depend on $\beta$. The matrix $K^TVK$ may be singular; positive definiteness is a separate hypothesis when a density is needed.
thm-gaussian-conditional-law-of-random-e:
## Statement

Assume AC and the Gaussian branch of the finite-dimensional mixed model. Let $V=ZGZ^T+R$ be positive definite. With conditional expectation taken componentwise given $\sigma(Y)$, and conditional covariance defined entrywise by conditional expectations of centered products, one has
$$
\mathbb E[b\mid Y]=GZ^TV^{-1}(Y-X\beta),\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(b\mid Y)=G-GZ^TV^{-1}ZG.
$$
The latent covariance $G$ may be singular.
thm-variance-component-identifiability-i:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\Theta$ be a nonempty parameter set and let $\theta\mapsto(G_\theta,R_\theta)$ be a declared covariance-component parameterization of the Gaussian mixed model, with
$$
V_\theta=ZG_\theta Z^T+R_\theta
$$
positive semidefinite for every $\theta\in\Theta$. Consider the parametric family
$$
P_{\beta,\theta}=N_n(X\beta,V_\theta),\qquad (\beta,\theta)\in\mathbb R^p\times\Theta,
$$
and the estimand $\psi(\beta,\theta)=\theta$. Then $\psi$ is identifiable if and only if the covariance map $\theta\mapsto V_\theta$ is injective on $\Theta$.
def-restricted-maximum-likelihood-error-:
## Definition

Assume AC and a Gaussian family of the form in [[def-gaussian-linear-mixed-model]], indexed by a nonempty parameter set $\Theta$. For each $\theta\in\Theta$, let $G_\theta$ and $R_\theta$ be the latent and residual covariance matrices in
$$
V_\theta=ZG_\theta Z^T+R_\theta\succ0.
$$
Let the fixed design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank with $p<n$. Fix an error-contrast matrix $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-p)}$ as in [[def-error-contrast-matrix]], independently of $\theta$. By [[lem-gaussian-error-contrast-is-multivariate-normal]], the contrast vector $K^TY$ has law $N_{n-p}(0,K^TV_\theta K)$ and its law does not depend on the fixed-effect parameter $\beta$. The local result [[lem-reml-error-contrast-covariance-is-positive-definite]] shows that this covariance is positive definite, and [[thm-nondegenerate-multivariate-normal-law-has-density]] gives its Gaussian density. The **restricted likelihood for this fixed contrast basis** is
$$
L_R(\theta;y)=(2\pi)^{-(n-p)/2}\det(K^TV_\theta K)^{-1/2}
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(K^Ty)^T(K^TV_\theta K)^{-1}(K^Ty)\right).
$$
This item defines the likelihood for a fixed, parameter-independent choice of contrast coordinates; it makes no claim about likelihood comparisons across different fixed-effect designs.
thm-known-covariance-gls-is-blue:
## Statement

Let the linear mixed model have fixed design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ of full column rank and known marginal covariance $V=\operatorname{Cov}(Y)\succ0$. Then
$$
\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{GLS}}=(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}X^TV^{-1}Y
$$
is unbiased for $\beta$, has covariance $(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}$, and is BLUE: for every linear unbiased estimator $\widetilde\beta$ and every $c\in\mathbb R^p$,
$$
\operatorname{Var}(c^T\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{GLS}})\le
\operatorname{Var}(c^T\widetilde\beta).
$$
Only the fixed-design mean and covariance are used; Gaussianity is not assumed.
lem-reml-error-contrast-basis-change-is-:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank with $p<n$, and let $K,K'\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-p)}$ be two error-contrast matrices for $X$. For every covariance parameter $\theta$ in [[def-restricted-maximum-likelihood-error-contrasts]], there is an invertible matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{(n-p)\times(n-p)}$, independent of $\theta$, such that $K'=KA$ and
$$
L_R^{K'}(\theta;y)=|\det A|^{-1}L_R^K(\theta;y)
$$
for every response vector $y$. Thus changing the fixed contrast basis multiplies the likelihood by a positive factor independent of the covariance parameter and leaves its maximizers unchanged.
thm-known-covariance-blup-for-random-eff:
## Statement

In the moment-only linear mixed model, suppose $X$ has full column rank and the known marginal covariance $V=ZGZ^T+R$ is positive definite. Define
$$
\widehat b=GZ^TV^{-1}(Y-X\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{GLS}}),\qquad
\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{GLS}}=(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}X^TV^{-1}Y.
$$
Here **best linear unbiased predictor (BLUP)** means that $\widehat b$ is unbiased for $\mathbb E b=0$ for every fixed $\beta$ and its prediction-error covariance is minimal in positive-semidefinite order among all affine linear predictors $a+BY$ with that same unbiasedness property. Then $\widehat b$ is a BLUP and
$$
\operatorname{Cov}(b-\widehat b)=G-GZ^TV^{-1}ZG+
GZ^TV^{-1}X(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}X^TV^{-1}ZG.
$$
No Gaussianity or Axiom of Choice is assumed. The covariance formula treats $G$ and $R$ as known; it does not cover the extra uncertainty from estimating variance components.
